hints.title: Max-Min Water Distance Obstacle
hints.text: Finding a water cell that maximizes distance to nearest land by running path searches from each 0 cell checks identical cells repeatedly. How can starting from all land cells simultaneously find the deepest ocean level?

hints.title: Outward Land Wave Invariant
hints.text: Enqueuing all land cells initially and expanding outward guarantees that the last water cell reached by the wavefront has the maximum distance to any land.

hints.title: Multi-Source Wave Level Procedure
hints.text: Collect all land cells (grid[r][c] == 1) in a queue. If all cells are land or all are water, return -1. While the queue has elements, iterate level by level, popping cells and expanding into adjacent 0 cells, marking them as 1 so they are not revisited. Track step distance and return step count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: grid width and height (1 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Every cell is enqueued and processed once in at most O(N^2) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Independent searches from each water cell take O(N^4) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place grid cell marking avoids allocating separate visited structures.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Returning -1 when grid contains all land (no water) or all water (no land).
